question:
(a) Explain the role of scattering of light in the colour of the sky.
(b) Predict the colour of the sky as seen from a place where there is no atmosphere. Justify your answer.

options.A:
(a) Air molecules and fine particles scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly, so blue light reaches the observer from many directions and the sky appears blue.
(b) Without an atmosphere there would be no particles to scatter sunlight into the line of sight away from the Sun, so the sky would appear dark or black.
options.B:
(a) The sky is blue because blue has the longest wavelength and is least scattered.
(b) Without an atmosphere the sky would become bright blue because sunlight travels freely.
options.C:
(a) Sky colour is due to refraction of sunlight through air only.
(b) Without atmosphere, the sky would be white because all colours remain mixed.
options.D:
(a) Air molecules scatter all colours equally, making the sky blue.
(b) Without atmosphere, the sky would appear red.
